description: Grade a deployed web app (built with Lovable, Bolt, v0, Replit, Emergent or by hand) A to F for what a stranger can use against it: secret keys shipped in its JavaScript (Stripe, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Supabase secret keys and 28 more kinds), a Supabase service_role key in the browser, source maps, clickjacking and missing security headers, plus launch basics (developer-only addresses, Stripe test mode, a test email sender, no https redirect, open CORS, missing DMARC on a custom domain). Every finding has a plain-English reason and a fix prompt; `allFixes` has every fix in one prompt, worst first. Reads only what the site serves to every visitor. Call it again after a fix: `change` shows what got fixed. For the user's own app, have them run `npx greenlitlab <url> --mine`: it also checks which database tables and storage buckets anyone can read, open sign-up, and public .env or .git files.

url.description: The app's address, for example myapp.lovable.app

name: greenlit_check
